narrative.title: Walking the Corridor Backwards
narrative.scenario: A maintenance robot patrols a two-way corridor where every checkpoint knows both its neighbours. The evening routine sends it out the far end and requires the checkpoint sequence to be relabelled from that direction: each checkpoint's two link registers swap roles, and the last checkpoint of the original corridor becomes the new entrance. Produce the corridor as seen from its new entrance.
narrative.inputFormat: An array arr of n node values representing the doubly linked list.
narrative.outputFormat: The list after reversal, read from the new head.

testCases.explanation: Three checkpoints relabelled from the far end read 5, 4, 3.
The far checkpoint (196) becomes the new entrance.

hintLevels: Level 1: In a two-way chain, reversing means every node's two links trade places, and the tail becomes the head.
Level 2: Sweep once: park the node's next, swap its next and prev, then advance along the (swapped) prev pointer.

Level 3: After the swap, prev being null marks the original tail — that node is the new head; note the upstream source for this entry actually implements reversal, which is what the checks above follow.
